content.text: Invariants are missing to bridge to the postcondition.

input.command:
cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "invariant",
 "proof_obligation": "bridge",
 "diagnosis": "The loop only has the bounds invariant 0 <= lo <= hi <= a.Length; the invariants saying K is not in a[..lo] (all a[j] < K for j < lo) and not in a[hi..] (all a[j] > K for j >= hi) are missing/commented out. So on exit with lo >= hi, Dafny cannot conclude that no index holds K, and the 'return false' path fails the ensures b == exists i :: a[i] == K."}
EOF
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='program.dfy'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("    //invariant forall j:nat :: j < lo ==> a[j] < K\n","    invariant forall j:nat :: j < lo ==> a[j] < K\n    invariant forall j:nat :: hi <= j < a.Length ==> a[j] > K\n")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
dafny verify program.dfy

content.text:
`program.dfy` now verifies: `dafny verify` reports 3 verified, 0 errors.

**Diagnosis** (written to `diagnosis.json`): the problem was a missing loop invariant, and the failing step was the bridge from the loop to the postcondition. The loop only kept track of the bounds `0 <= lo <= hi <= a.Length`. It said nothing about which parts of the array had been ruled out, and the invariant that would have covered that was commented out. So when the loop ended with `lo >= hi`, Dafny couldn't conclude that `K` appears nowhere in the array, and the `return false` path failed `ensures b == exists i :: ... a[i] == K`. The counterexample shows this: `K` sits in the last element, `a[2437]`, but the proof had no way to say that this element had been checked.

**Fix:** I made two changes to the loop invariants in `program.dfy`:
- I uncommented the existing invariant `forall j:nat :: j < lo ==> a[j] < K`, so every element below `lo` is known to be less than `K`.
- I added `forall j:nat :: hi <= j < a.Length ==> a[j] > K`, so every element from `hi` onward is known to be greater than `K`.

When the loop ends, `lo >= hi`, so these two facts cover the whole array and show that `K` isn't in it, which proves the `return false` path. Both invariants stay true through each step because the array is sorted (`isSorted`). I didn't change the method's `requires` or `ensures`.
